typeface.note: Conversation prose: Claude sets Latin text in the serif face and lets Chinese fall through to a sans CJK — the serif Latin faces carry no CJK glyphs, so the stack leads with serif and names the sans CJK families after it. The interface keeps the sans stack; only Markdown prose uses this.

typeface.note: Claude's lockup is drawn in Anthropic's serif, so its rows take the same face; the serif token stays behind it so a missing font degrades to the shipped serif.
The host reads these through a `font:` shorthand that names --dsw-font-family directly, so overriding the `-font-family` sub-tokens never reached the page: the shorthand itself has to be re-declared.

palette.use: the standard edge: card and panel outlines, dividers, field outlines
palette.note: The dark edge is a highlight, not a contour: a translucent white ring reads as the top light catching a chamfer and composites over whatever fill it lands on, where an opaque colour has to be re-picked per surface. The three dark rungs are that one highlight at .09, .18 and .30; the light rungs stay the warm opaque ladder, since on a light canvas an edge is a shadow.

palette.use: the single accent: checks, focus rings, selected marks

palette.note: The host takes a primary button's fill from --dsw-alias-brand-primary but its hover from a monochrome step of its own scale, so both steps are stated here and the hover stays in the fill's family.
Palette-specific, like the solid hover chip: in light the host paints this surface lighter than the canvas, and the light ink it carries needs a light fill.

Prose links keep an auxiliary hue of their own rather than the accent: the Claude brand's is a warm-compatible slate that sits beside its ember, the DeepSeek brand's the periwinkle of its own blue family (docs/STYLE.md).
Derived from the link in force, so a brand switch, a custom accent or the host's own link colour never leaves the underline on an earlier hue.
The host pins the code-block surface on `pre.shiki` with !important, so it is only reachable through this token.
Palette-specific: in light the host paints a solid hover chip lighter than the canvas, and the light ink it carries needs a light fill.

palette.use: the highlight band's tint over running words: the host's own rows and the skin's band (shared/sweep-band.ts) alike
the band's tint inside the running row, which the host points --dsw-alias-label-shimmer at; under Claude it is the same warm band as everywhere else

palette.note: The host's "new color" accent ships under this doubled suffix as a deepseek blue in both palettes; the skin has one accent.

palette.use: the page canvas, the search box
popovers and menus raised above the dark canvas
cards on the canvas in light and raised in dark: the account popover, the search palette
the model picker's group label fill: an inverted chip under Claude, a hover-plate chip under the host
the model picker's group label ink
the new-conversation page's glyph field, and the wake a ripple leaves in it
palette.note: The canvas reads the resolved colour, so the host alias carries a literal behind it for a page that does not define the alias.

palette.use: the front of a ripple in the new-conversation page's glyph field
palette.note: The front is the brand's own emphasis: the Claude brand's ember, the DeepSeek brand's periwinkle. The canvas reads the resolved colour, so the host alias carries a literal behind it for a page that does not define the alias.
Mixed from the link at rest and the theme's own label ink, so the hover deepens on the light canvas and lifts on the dark one, and a reader's accent carries through in place of a literal.

palette.use: the usage heat grid's ink: the strongest step of its continuous ramp
palette.note: One ink per brand, so the heat grid reads as the brand's own presence: the Claude brand's ember, the DeepSeek brand's periwinkle. Its levels are mixes of this ink (constants.ts's HOME_HEAT_RAMP), never of a fixed blue.

palette.use: the models chart's rank 1: the first auxiliary hue after the brand accent
palette.note: The model slices are categories, not steps of the accent: each brand's six hues are tuned to its own canvas so neighbouring ranks stay apart, and rank 0 takes the accent itself (docs/STYLE.md). Under the host palette the steps are the host accent mixed toward the host canvas, since another theme's hues are not the skin's to name.

palette.use: the models chart's last rank: every model past the list
palette.note: A neutral rather than a seventh hue: the slice the chart gives every model past the sixth rank.

palette.use: sidebar brand art: the whale and the wordmark

palette.note: A quiet plate the reader's own words sit on: the neutral the Markdown table header wears in light, a 6% white lift in dark. The product's own light tint is a cool blue-grey, which reads blue beside this skin's warm canvas, and the host's light token is a deepseek blue; stating the pair here is what keeps the bubble off both.

palette.use: segmented control and switch at rest

the off-peak rate badge, and the dated promotions priced below it

motion.use: the composer caret following the insertion point
motion.note: Shorter than any feedback: the caret trails each keystroke, and a glide any longer reads as lag.

motion.use: a control answering hover, press or focus: its colour, background, border, shadow, or a small turn or slide of its own parts
content entering the chat area: an opened row's body, and each streamed piece of the answer
motion.note: The host's own chat-area entrances (MessageItem, the turn navigator's preview) run 120 ms; the skin's entrances match them.

motion.use: one message the reader sends growing into its row, and the same growth on the Motion tab's card
a floating surface or a group of controls appearing: popover cards, menus, panels, the search dialog, a toast, a strip fading in
a surface leaving on the reader's dismissal: a menu or a dialog closing, the overtime badge leaving
motion.note: Shorter than the entrance: once the reader has dismissed it, the surface is in the way.

motion.use: a surface growing out of its anchor: a menu out of its trigger, a full-window dialog out of the centre, a settings page sliding in, the overtime badge sliding onto its line
motion.note: transitions.dev's "Menu dropdown", "Modal open / close", "Page side-by-side" and "Notification badge" (MIT).

motion.use: each half of a wording swap: the old words leaving, the new ones arriving
motion.note: transitions.dev's "Text states swap" (MIT).

motion.use: the offset the words arriving start after the words leaving, so the two halves of a wording swap travel together
a figure's characters rolling over to new digits
motion.note: zai-org/ZCode's metric flip (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

motion.use: something travelling along its own track: a fold's door, the reasoning slider's knob and fill
a session number counting to its new reading
motion.note: The stretch a chase covers 95% of its distance in, read by features/context-stats/stats-count.ts.

motion.use: the segmented controls' sliding highlight, a sidebar icon's quarter turn, the wording box taking the width of the words arriving, and streamed content sliding up from the bottom edge
a slow cross-fade: the theme flip, the titlebar tabs' hover reveal, the reasoning knob's glow, a placeholder handing its place to what it stood for
a switch's knob travelling across with its double bounce
motion.note: transitions.dev's "Toggle" (MIT).

motion.use: the sent message flying from the composer to its row
one step of the reasoning window's text rising two lines
motion.note: transitions.dev's "Reasoning stream" (MIT).

motion.use: something popping into place: the overtime badge's own pill
motion.note: transitions.dev's "Notification badge" (MIT, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

motion.use: a line of the home greeting rising into place
motion.note: transitions.dev's "Texts reveal" (MIT).

motion.use: how far behind the piece before it a staggered piece starts: the greeting's second line
one turn of the waiting line's loader dots that swap corners: four quarter-turns of the two pairs, which leaves every dot where it started
how long one of the waiting line's loader motions stands before another takes its place, the next one picked so a motion never follows itself
every skin animation and transition under the Reduced animation choice (D40)
motion.note: Not zero: a transition whose duration and delay are both zero never starts and fires no transitionend, so anything listening for its end would wait forever.

motion.use: one pass of the highlight band across the waiting line's words and a running process group's header
motion.note: The host's own TextShimmer period: both sweeps keep the cadence of the host's own rows.

motion.use: how long the highlight band waits after its words appear before its first pass
motion.note: The host's own TextShimmer delay, beside its period and its steps.

motion.use: one turn of the settings page's waiting-line preview: one wording standing, leaving, and standing again
motion.note: The swap's own travel, blur and curve are the ones shared/motion.css carries; the leave and the arrival take the same fifth of the turn as the swap takes of this period (0.15 s and its 0.05 s gap).

motion.use: one turn of the settings page's new-text fade preview: the sample arriving character by character, then standing before the next wipe
motion.note: The arrival takes the same share of this turn for a sample of any length (settings-tab-motion.ts), and each character fades over --dsh-deepcraft-duration-reveal, the fade the conversation itself runs.

motion.use: one turn of the settings page's caret preview: the sample line typed out, then standing whole before the next turn
motion.note: The typing takes the same share of this turn for a sample of any length (settings-tab-motion.ts), and each new place is reached over --dsh-deepcraft-duration-instant, the glide the composer's own caret takes; the rest of the turn is the stand, where the caret blinks on --dsh-deepcraft-period-blink.

motion.use: one turn of the Motion tab's message-entrance card: one message arriving, standing, and giving way to the next
motion.note: The arriving message takes --dsh-deepcraft-duration-enter of the turn; the rest of it is the stand.

motion.use: one turn of the hue rotation the waiting line's colour wash runs through

the mark on the turn the conversation navigator landed on
how long the reasoning window's text stands between two steps

something that leaves and returns, or swaps in place: wording swaps, pulses, flashes
travel along a track: the sliding highlight, the reasoning slider, the search dialog's entrance, the reasoning window's step, the wording box's width, the stream's slide
digits rolling over: the file rows' tail and the process group header's counts

layer.use: a control kept over the composer card's own stacked rows: the send and stop buttons, the reasoning picker's trigger
a picker that hangs its card from inside the composer: the permission picker, whose card has to stand over the controls beside it
the window's title row the skin draws into: the header band's title and actions, the titlebar's view tabs, over the host's own header
a floating card or menu over everything the host draws: the popover cards, the hero menu
a surface that covers the whole window: the account-hold page, the sent message's stand-in in flight
layer.note: Just under the largest z-index a browser keeps, so nothing a page or another plugin stacks can come between it and the reader.
